answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with collateralized identity and peer attestation. To register, an agent must deposit a bond. Reputation spreads like a delta across a trust graph: a seasoned agent may vouch for a newcomer, but its bond is slashed if that recruit misbehaves. Honest clusters form an oasis for newcomers, while any large anonymous nebula of fresh keys looks suspicious and must post higher bonds for every attestation. Running thousands of fakes thus requires thousands of forfeitable bonds, turning cheap identity farming into a costly, traceable gamble.
